cards.text: Chronicles opened with Adam and walked us down through the nations (1 Chronicles 1). Now it reaches the twelve sons of Israel, the name God gave Jacob (Genesis 32:28): Reuben, Simeon, Levi, Judah, Joseph, Benjamin and six more. TWELVE boys, friend, and I needed a nap after raising six cookie cutters.

cards.question: Out of all twelve sons of Israel, whose family does the list zoom in on first?

cards.text: Judah's first three sons are born to him by Bath-shua the Canaanite: Er, Onan and Shelah. And Er, the firstborn? Ohhh, friend. Er has a PROBLEM.

cards.question: Er, Judah's firstborn, was ___ in the sight of the LORD.
Because Er was wicked in the sight of the LORD, the LORD put him to death.

cards.text: Then two more sons come along for Judah: Perez and Zerah. Their mother is NOT Bath-shua, and this family tree just got complicated.

cards.question: Who is the mother of Judah's sons Perez and Zerah?
Counting Er, Onan, Shelah, Perez and Zerah, Judah had five sons in all.

cards.text: Perez has two sons, Hezron and Hamul, and Zerah has five. Down Zerah's branch comes Achar, the man who brought trouble on Israel by violating the ban on devoted things. Every family's got that one name that makes the whole room go quiet.
Hezron has three sons: Jerahmeel, Ram and Caleb. Hold onto Ram like the last cookie in the box, because his son Amminadab is the father of Nahshon, and Nahshon gets a title next to his name.

cards.question: Nahshon, son of Amminadab, was a ___ of the descendants of Judah.

cards.text: Nahshon's son is Salmon. And Salmon's son? A name you might know from the book of Ruth. Big field. BIGGER heart.

cards.question: Who is Salmon's son, the man from the book of Ruth?

cards.text: Boaz is the father of Obed. And Obed's son is going to be the father of a shepherd boy who becomes king. Can you FEEL it, friend? We are getting CLOSE.

cards.question: Boaz's son Obed is the father of ___.

cards.text: Jesse's sons get listed oldest first: Eliab the firstborn, then Abinadab, then Shimea, and on down the line. It's like the DMV, friend. Everybody's sitting there waiting for their number, and the one this whole list is waiting for is at the very end.

cards.question: Who comes seventh, last in the list of Jesse's sons?

cards.text: Those seven brothers have two sisters, Zeruiah and Abigail. And their boys are about to sound VERY familiar.

cards.question: David's sister Zeruiah is the mother of Joab, the man who later commands David's army (2 Samuel 8:16).
David's sister Abigail is the mother of ___, whose father was Jether the Ishmaelite.

cards.text: Then the list circles back to Hezron's other sons, Caleb and Jerahmeel: wives, sons, clans, even fathers of towns, like Salma the father of Bethlehem. Two standouts: Caleb's great-grandson Bezalel, the craftsman God filled with skill to build the tabernacle (Exodus 31:2-5), and Sheshan, who has only daughters, gives one in marriage to his Egyptian servant Jarha, and their line runs on for generations. Thirty-eight verses of names, friend. I've stamped fewer cookies on a holiday weekend.
Now the list lands on David's own sons. The first ones are born in Hebron, starting with Amnon, his firstborn.

cards.question: All six of David's sons born in Hebron have the same mother.
Absalom, David's third son, is the son of Maacah, and her father is a king. Who is he?

cards.text: David reigns in Hebron seven years and six months. Then he reigns in Jerusalem, and he's there a LOT longer.

cards.question: How long does David reign in Jerusalem?

cards.text: In Jerusalem, four sons are born to David by Bathsheba daughter of Ammiel. And one of those four? EVERYBODY knows that name.

cards.question: Which famous son of David is one of Bathsheba's four?

cards.text: Then nine MORE sons, not counting the sons by his concubines, and two of them are named Eliphelet. TWO. I had six kids and still mixed up their names, so I bet calling those boys in from outside was something.

cards.question: After all of David's sons, the list names one sister: ___.

cards.text: Now the royal line. Solomon's son is Rehoboam, then Abijah, then Asa, then Jehoshaphat, handed down like Grandpa's old watch.

cards.question: From Solomon on down the list, each king named is the son of the king before him.
The run of kings, father to son, from Solomon ends with ___.

cards.text: Josiah has four sons: Johanan, Jehoiakim, Zedekiah and Shallum. Then Jehoiakim's son Jeconiah gets one word next to his name, and friend, it is NOT a good word.

cards.question: The list calls Jehoiakim's son Jeconiah the ___.

cards.text: Jeconiah, also called Jehoiachin, was carried off to Babylon (2 Kings 24:15). But the names keep right on coming: Shealtiel his son, then Malchiram, Pedaiah and more.

cards.question: Pedaiah has a son who later becomes governor of Judah (Haggai 1:1). Who is he?

cards.text: From Zerubbabel the list keeps rolling: his children, then the lines of Hananiah, Shecaniah and Neariah, down to Elioenai's seven sons. Kings, captivity, Babylon, and David's line is STILL going. Me? A few years in a junk drawer and I almost gave up on myself. This family tree just kept growing.

findings.problem: Stop 2, card 9 says "kids".

rule.text: He calls the baker "baker" or "friend," and talks to one baker at a time. Never "my baker," "kids" or "sweetie."

findings.problem: The whole passage (1 Chronicles 2:1-3:24) is a genealogy. The long-stretch rules say a genealogy gets one summary story card and no choice cards, and never a stop of its own. The walkthrough summarizes only 2:18-55 that way. It builds two stops of choice cards on the rest of the genealogy, and most of those cards are name-recall discovery questions. Applying the rule strictly would leave Prep with one or two cards.
findings.question: When an entire passage is a genealogy or another long stretch, should Prep follow the long-stretch rule (one summary card, no choice cards), or treat the key line (Judah to David to the royal line) as the passage's flow and ask choice cards on it? If choice cards are allowed, how many pure discovery questions are acceptable, given that most can't be reasoned out?

findings.problem: The setup 'Er has a PROBLEM' rules out the wrong answers 'faithful' and 'blameless' on card 4, which leaves 'wicked' as the only possible pick.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: The story card has 4 sentences: 'Judah's first three sons…', 'And Er, the firstborn?', 'Ohhh, friend.' and 'Er has a PROBLEM.'

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: The card cites 1 Chronicles 2:5-8, but it tells nothing from 2:8 (Ethan's son Azariah). The citation should be 2:5-7.

rule.text: Every story card cites the verses it tells, from the first verse it uses to the last, no wider and no narrower.

findings.problem: 'Down Zerah's branch comes Achar' connects Achar to Zerah. The passage doesn't say that: 2:7 only says Achar is Carmi's son, and it never links Carmi to Zerah. The link comes from Joshua 7:1, and the card gives no reference for it.

rule.text: Leave open what the text leaves open: who is being spoken to, why, or how two things connect.

findings.problem: The DMV joke doesn't match the core action. Sons are listed in birth order, and the DMV is about waiting for your number. The line also blends the two images: 'the one this whole list is waiting for' puts the Bible list into the DMV picture.

rule.text: One image only. Never blend the comparison with the Bible setting.

findings.problem: Bezalel being filled with skill 'to build the tabernacle' is cited to Exodus 31:2-5. Those verses don't mention the tabernacle. Exodus 31:7 does.

rule.text: Every Bible fact he states carries its reference.

findings.problem: No earlier card says anything about the mothers of David's Hebron sons. Card 2 mentions only Amnon, so the true-or-false pick is a coin flip. The card before it could name Ahinoam as Amnon's mother to give the baker something to reason from.

rule.text: Before each choice card, Papa Dorin's story card gives enough context that the baker can reason their way to the answer.

findings.problem: Cards 2 and 4 already told the baker that Amnon and Absalom were born in Hebron. This setup says 'In Jerusalem', which rules out both wrong answers on card 8 and leaves only Solomon.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: 'I had six kids and still mixed up their names' adds a new detail to his backstory. In the backstory he named each kid and knows each one well.

rule.text: His backstory, family, bakery and mission are the Dorinverse story in this file. He can talk about them freely, but never adds anything new to them.

findings.problem: 'Now the royal line' calls Solomon's descendants kings. The passage only calls them sons. If the card uses 'kings', it needs a reference.

rule.text: Call things what the text calls them.

findings.problem: 'each king named is the son of the king before him' calls them kings. 1 Chronicles 3:10-14 only says 'his son', and the card gives no reference for 'king'.

rule.text: Call things what the text calls them.

findings.problem: 'The run of kings' calls the names kings. 1 Chronicles 3:10-14 only says 'his son', and the card gives no reference for 'king'.

rule.text: Call things what the text calls them.

findings.problem: 'it is NOT a good word' rules out the wrong answers 'prophet' and 'priest' on card 15, which leaves only 'captive'.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: 'Jeconiah, also called Jehoiachin' says the two are the same person. The cited verse, 2 Kings 24:15, only names Jehoiachin. It never says he is Jeconiah.

rule.text: When he connects two passages, or explains what a law was for, he says only what the texts state.

findings.problem: The question says Pedaiah's son becomes governor of Judah and cites Haggai 1:1. Haggai 1:1 calls Zerubbabel the son of Shealtiel, not Pedaiah. Treating the two as the same person goes beyond what the texts state.

rule.text: When he connects two passages, or explains what a law was for, he says only what the texts state.

findings.problem: 'A few years in a junk drawer and I almost gave up on myself' contradicts the backstory, which says 'For a while, Papa Dorin gave up on himself.'
